### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/metadata: patch`, no `!`, no `**BREAKING**` paragraph, no ADR-0087 marker; `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` on the changeset and the PR body. This is the right level and the right arm.

The arm, FROM → TO: rows 1 and 2 are a `409` that becomes an answer; row 3 is a `409` whose candidate list loses the host's package. No answer becomes a refusal and no read naming a package moves, so no `(narrowing)` arm applies. The siblings that carry one each add a refusal (#32676 `no (narrowing)`, #32740 `yes (narrowing)`). A refusal that becomes an answer is declared `yes (widening)` in this repository when the refusal has shipped (changesets 30025, 31264). Here it has not: the refusal is #32560's, whose note is still pending, as are the per-package slot notes it rests on, and the released `@objectstack/metadata` 18.3.0 carries no per-package slot. The refusal and its removal first ship in the same release, so no released accept set widens (the same reasoning as `.changeset/30091-data-key-trial-page.md`). The line argues `no` from D4 alone and should also say this (N4). `Metadata-protocol: none` is right: nothing an author writes changes. No export is added to the package's public surface (`packagelessWriteKeyOf` is not exported from `index.ts`).

The arm stays `no` after B1 and B2 are fixed as measured below: both fixes return cells to a refusal main already gives or to the answer before #32560.

- The PR is a draft opened by the fleet bot; auto-merge is not armed.
- **Landing order with #32676.** As committed, the two heads together fail #32676's loose C3 `action` block. Whichever lands second must carry the tightening. The claim says this PR lands first and #32676 tightens after; if #32676 landed first, this PR's merge-queue build would be red.
- `main` has moved to `1ec547fc`. One of its commits (`5defbfeb9`, #31698) touches `metadata-manager.ts` (it adds `unregisterInMemory` and a registry-only cluster removal). The head merges with it without conflict (`git merge-tree`); nothing was run on that merge.

### ④ Design judgment

The fix corrects the count at read time and leaves the cause in place: the boot pass stamps a stored package-less row with the host's package and files it in the host's registry slot. Three consequences follow.

- The set-aside rests on object identity (a `WeakSet` of the objects `loadMany` handed out). It holds for the boot state. After one package-less write of the name the host's slot holds a body that is not a recorded row, and the phantom host is back (S2). The same happens when the row leaves the table behind the manager (the declared limit).
- The read and the removal now disagree in row 1's composition: the bare read answers the package-less row, and the bare removal is still refused naming the host's package (S1 d).
- The rule "a package slot whose item is a recorded row is not a holder" is wider than "the slot the host's stamp filled". It also matches a package's own slot that the registry's write rule filled with the row as that package's customization (B2).

Withholding the stamp from a stored row at the pass, which #32676's D1 guard already does for a name two packages hold, would remove the phantom at its source for reads, removals and later writes alike. That is a design question for the epic #31527 seat and is not asked of this PR. Within this PR's design, the filing itself (`packagelessWriteKeyOf` shared with `storeWriteKey`) agrees with D4's write rule.

### Findings

**B1 — must-fix. One package that binds the name to two objects, with a package-less row saved last: the bare read answers that package's other row.** Host declaring `com.host.app`.

| Stored rows, in save order | before #32560 | main | this head |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| ALPHA@account, ALPHA@contact, package-less@account | the package-less row | `409` host, alpha, environment | ALPHA's contact row |
| ALPHA (object-less), ALPHA@account, package-less (object-less) | the package-less row | `409` host, alpha, environment | ALPHA's account row |

With the two ALPHA rows saved in the other order this head answers the package-less row, and on a host declaring no package or ALPHA all three trees answer it. So the answer on this head is not the row saved last, and it depends on the host's package, which is what the card set out to remove. Cause: the refactor `268cb2e2d` dropped the write order of the filed row; it sits in the view with no order, and `writtenLast` then returns the view's last key. With `8937cda1e`'s two source files both cells answer the package-less row and nothing else in the probe differs. The PR body's acceptance note says no composition measured reads "written last" across the filed row; this one does. The changeset's Clause-② line says the read goes "to the package-less row, the answer before the bare read was judged over the loaders"; here it goes to neither. Fix: give the filed row the write order of the registry slot it came from (the first commit did), and pin both cells.

**B2 — must-fix. A package's own slot that holds the row as its customization is set aside too, and the bare read then answers the package-less row where two packages hold the name.** Host declaring no package, so no stamp is involved.

| Composition | before #32560 | main | this head |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| ALPHA's action registered in memory before the pass; the table holds BETA's row and a package-less row saved last | the package-less row | `409` alpha, beta, environment | the package-less row |
| ALPHA's action registered in memory before the pass; the table holds the package-less row; BETA's action registered in memory after the pass | `409` alpha, beta | `409` alpha, beta, environment | the package-less row |

In both, the pass registers the package-less row and the registry's own write rule files it in ALPHA's slot, ALPHA being the one holder then (D4). `slotViewOf` sets that slot aside because its item is a recorded row a loader still stores, ALPHA is no longer counted, and the row is filed as BETA's customization. A read naming ALPHA answers the row and a read naming BETA answers BETA's item, so two packages hold the name and the bare read picks (red line 2). The changeset says "Unchanged: a host declaring no package"; both cells move against main, and the second also against the tree before #32560. Measured variant: set the slot aside only when the row carries that slot's package as its stamp (`indexedItemPackageId(data) === slotPackageOf(key)`). The two cells return to main's `409`, and the other 101 cells of that probe file and the file's 158 tests do not move. The variant was not measured together with B1's fix. Reach: no first-party caller registers an `action` in memory, so first-party 0, like every row of the card. Pin both cells.

**S1 — should-fix, in the same round: the changeset's and PR body's text.**
(a) "Unchanged: … the holder's own package" does not hold for ALPHA@account, BETA@contact and an object-less package-less row on a host declaring ALPHA: `409` alpha, beta → `409` alpha, beta, environment. The same rows on a host declaring `com.host.app` go from `409` host, alpha, beta to `409` alpha, beta, environment, which row 3 covers only if it says the environment may be added.
(b) A holder that is in memory only, beside the stamped row (the table holds the package-less row; ALPHA's action is registered in memory): before #32560 `409` host, alpha; main `409` host, alpha, environment; this head the package-less row. That is right by D4, but it is not "the answer before the bare read was judged over the loaders", and no row declares it.
(c) "a host's own item registered in memory, which is still a holder" holds for an item registered after the pass. One registered before it is replaced in the host's slot by the stamped row, and the bare read answers the package-less row (as before #32560; main named the host). State the scope.
(d) State that in row 1's composition the removal naming no package is still refused naming the host's package, so the read and the removal now disagree there, until the removal card lands.
(e) Rows 1 and 2 also cover a package-less row bound to an object (three more cells, same move); say so.
